products.name: Obsidian AI
products.note: Local-first knowledge AI; plugins; privacy-focused; no cloud dependency

reading.body:
Obsidian's AI strategy centers on local-first processing: all computation happens on the user's device with no data sent to Obsidian's servers, reversing the cloud-dependent model that dominates AI products.

This approach trades cloud infrastructure costs for client-side compute. The user's machine becomes the binding resource instead of server capacity and bandwidth. The two registered MCP servers suggest the company is enabling AI assistants to access Obsidian vaults through standard protocols, but the fundamental claim remains that processing stays local. For builders of AI systems, this means Obsidian users cannot be counted as load on data center power budgets the way cloud-hosted AI products can be.

The data does not specify what compute requirements Obsidian AI actually demands on user devices, whether the model runs locally or calls remote APIs despite the privacy claim, or how the company monetizes a freemium product without the operational advantages of centralized compute. The local-first model works only if users have sufficient hardware, a constraint that differs from grid-dependent infrastructure but remains a constraint nonetheless.

profile_text.body:
Obsidian is a for-profit startup founded in 2020 and headquartered in Los Angeles, California, that makes a free, flexible note-taking and knowledge management application. The company describes its software as a private, local-first tool that stores notes directly on a user's device, accessible offline, with no server-side access even by Obsidian itself. The application supports personal notes, journaling, knowledge bases, and project management, and includes features such as bidirectional note linking, an interactive relationship graph, a limitless canvas for brainstorming, and an open plugin API with thousands of community extensions.

The site's held facts classify Obsidian's primary AI offering as Obsidian AI, categorized under notes, knowledge, and meetings, and described as a local-first knowledge AI that is privacy-focused and carries no cloud dependency. Two third-party MCP servers are registered against the product: one connects AI assistants to a GitHub-hosted Obsidian vault for access and search, and another allows AI assistants to search a vault by title or keyword and summarize related content. No litigation is recorded against the company, though California is noted as its primary legal exposure jurisdiction with 175 associated entries.
